captions.text: This lesson maintains an existing IC command board in a
fictional warehouse exercise.
The screens come from the same saved exercise across browser sessions.
Begin in Call Details and verify the Warehouse alarm
name and training location.
Active Command and Open Command Board identify the available
route into this incident.
Choose Open Command Board.
Check the incident name again on Command Board, along with
Wallace Boden as commander.
Before practicing, make this identity check a habit; similar lane names
can appear on different incidents.

Original speech words, cue bounds and source pixels remain unchanged. This is source/cue review only, not encoded-frame or browser playback approval.

scenes.title: Read the structure and resource pool

captions.text: Command Structure shows Search Division and Staging.
Squad 3 is already in Search Division; Staging has no assigned resource.
Rotate and Requirements are review cues on the saved assignment.
They do not move the unit automatically.
Scroll to Resources.
All is selected, with Unassigned and Assigned available beside it.
The pool contains Squad 3, Engine 51 and the fictional Exercise Gate Marshal.
Engine 51 names Christopher Herrmann in its Officer or Team Lead position while
the unit remains unassigned to a lane.
Crew membership and command allocation describe different things.
For practice, explain that difference before proposing a move.

scenes.title: Add a benchmark and record progress

captions.text: In Tactical Objectives, choose Add.
The empty section gives us a clear starting point.
In Add Objective, select Benchmark under Type and enter the training
primary-search objective.
Choose Add to save it.
A specific objective name gives the next operator something concrete to review.
Open the objective and use Progress to set fifty percent.
The returned details show fifty percent selected.
Outcome, Close-out note and Complete Objective describe a
separate close-out decision.
This exercise leaves the objective incomplete.
Practice updating progress without treating an estimate
as a completed search.
